headline: Funding flows. FCC approvals. Tactical collaborations.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic partnerships shaping the space landscape.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in a Series C round, valuing the company at $1.6B. The funding aims to bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, with a clear nod to increased DoD interest in these areas. This follows their recent contracts with the Pentagon, signaling a robust pull-through from government needs.
stories.soWhat: With cash flow now firmly in hand, True Anomaly may just become the go-to for co-orbital defense—if they can navigate the bureaucracy.

stories.head: Portal Space partners with Quindar for military missions
stories.body: Portal Space has enlisted Quindar for ground mission support as it prepares to launch its maneuverable spacecraft aimed at military applications. This partnership is part of a broader trend where startups are actively courting government contracts to solidify their market positions. The move aligns with the increasing military focus on agile space solutions.
stories.soWhat: If Portal can actually launch on time, they might just redefine military space operations—assuming they can maneuver through the red tape.

stories.head: Vast diversifies into high-power satellite buses
stories.body: Vast has announced a new line of high-power satellite buses, expanding beyond its initial focus on commercial space stations. This strategic pivot comes as the demand for robust satellite infrastructure continues to grow, particularly for national security missions. The company is aiming to capture a slice of the lucrative defense market.
stories.soWhat: Vast's shift suggests that even companies known for one thing are willing to pivot—perhaps a reminder that in space, versatility is key.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on FCC satellite approvals
watchlist.body: With Lynk Global's recent FCC nod for direct-to-device testing, expect more companies to push for regulatory green lights next week.

watchlist.title: Upcoming budget discussions on space resilience
watchlist.body: The $1.4B addition to the FY27 budget for space resilience could influence procurement strategies—watch for shifts in contractor priorities.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser development
watchlist.body: Having cleared its critical design review, the Dream Chaser DoD variant will be closely watched as it moves toward production—challenges ahead.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: With a $480M extension on the TITAN program, Palantir's role in military data operations will likely expand, impacting competitors in the space.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
